title.zh: 卷一百〇七 列傳第三十七: 列女
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 列傳第三十七: 列女 Volume 107 Biographies 37: Exemplary Women

sentences.zh: ○邢簡妻陳氏耶律氏常哥耶律奴妻蕭氏耶律朮者妻蕭氏耶律中妻蕭氏

translations.literal: ○ The wife of Xing Jian, Lady Chen; the Yelü clanswoman Changge; the wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao; the wife of Yelü Shuzhe, Lady Xiao; the wife of Yelü Zhong, Lady Xiao
translations.idiomatic: ○ Lady Chen, wife of Xing Jian; the Yelü clanswoman Changge; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Shuzhe; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Zhong

sentences.zh: 男女居室，人之大倫。

translations.literal: Men and women dwelling together is the great norm of humanity.
translations.idiomatic: The pairing of men and women in marriage is among the greatest norms of human life.

sentences.zh: 與其得烈女，不若得賢女。

translations.literal: Rather than obtaining a fierce/chaste woman, it is better to obtain a worthy woman.
translations.idiomatic: Better to gain a worthy woman than a woman celebrated chiefly for desperate virtue.

sentences.zh: 天下而有烈女之名，非幸也。

translations.literal: For all under Heaven to have the name of fierce/chaste women is not fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm must acclaim women chiefly for acts of desperate virtue, that is no blessing.

sentences.zh: 《詩》贊衛共姜，《春秋》褒宋伯姬，蓋不得已，所以重人倫之變也。

translations.literal: The Odes praise Wei Gong Jiang; the Spring and Autumn Annals commends Song Bo Ji — this is only when there is no alternative, thereby to emphasize changes in human norms.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs praises Wei Gong Jiang, and the Spring and Autumn Annals commends Song Bo Ji—each case arose only when there was no other choice, and thus marks how heavily human relations weigh when they are torn apart.

sentences.zh: 遼據北方，風化視中土為疏。

translations.literal: The Liao held the north; customs and transformation were regarded as looser than the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: With the Liao entrenched in the north, their norms of teaching and custom were held looser than those of the central plains.

sentences.zh: 終遼之世，得賢女二，烈女三，以見人心之天理有不與世道存亡者。

translations.literal: Throughout the Liao dynasty, there were obtained two worthy women and three fierce/chaste women, thereby to show that the heavenly principle in human hearts has something that does not rise and fall with worldly fortunes.
translations.idiomatic: Across the entire Liao dynasty, only two worthy women and three women of desperate virtue were found—enough to show that the moral principle in human hearts can outlast the fortunes of the age.

sentences.zh: 邢簡妻陳氏，營州人。

translations.literal: The wife of Xing Jian, Lady Chen, was a native of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, wife of Xing Jian, came from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父陘，五代時累官司徒。

translations.literal: Her father Chen Sui repeatedly held the office of Grand Preceptor during the Five Dynasties period.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chen Sui rose repeatedly to the post of Grand Preceptor under the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 陳氏甫笄，涉通經義，凡覽詩賦，輒能誦，尤好吟詠，時以女秀才名之。

translations.literal: When Lady Chen had just reached the age of pinning up her hair, she had thoroughly grasped the meaning of the classics; whenever she looked upon poetry and fu, she could at once recite them; she especially loved composing verse, and at the time she was styled the "female xiucai."
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Lady Chen came of age, she had mastered the classics; whatever poetry or fu she read, she could recite from memory; she loved composing verse above all, and people called her the "female scholar."

sentences.zh: 年二十，歸於簡。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty she was married to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty she married Xing Jian.

sentences.zh: 孝舅姑，閨門和睦，親黨推重。

translations.literal: She was filial toward her parents-in-law; the inner quarters were harmonious; relatives and associates held her in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: She was devoted to her parents-in-law, kept the household harmonious, and won the respect of kin and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 有六子，陳氏親教以經。

translations.literal: She had six sons; Lady Chen personally instructed them in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: She bore six sons and taught them the classics herself.

sentences.zh: 後二子抱樸、抱質皆以賢，位宰相。

translations.literal: Later two of her sons, Baopu and Baozhi, both proved worthy and reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Two of her sons, Baopu and Baozhi, later proved themselves worthy men and rose to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 統和十二年卒。

translations.literal: She died in the twelfth year of the Tonghe reign period.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the twelfth year of Tonghe (994).

sentences.zh: 睿智皇后聞之，嗟悼，贈魯國夫人，刻石以表其行。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ruizhi heard of it, she sighed and mourned, bestowed upon her the title Lady of Lu, and had stone carved to commemorate her conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ruizhi heard of her death, she sighed in grief, granted her the title Lady of Lu, and had a stone inscription carved to commemorate her conduct.

sentences.zh: 及遷祔，遣使以祭。

translations.literal: When her remains were moved to joint entombment, the court sent an envoy to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When her remains were moved to joint burial with her husband, the court sent an envoy to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 論者謂貞靜柔順，婦道母儀始終無慊雲。

translations.literal: Commentators said she was chaste, quiet, gentle, and compliant—wifehood and motherhood in model form, from beginning to end without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said she was chaste, quiet, gentle, and compliant—a model of wifehood and motherhood from first to last, without a single lapse.

sentences.zh: 耶律氏，太師適魯之妹，小字常哥。

translations.literal: A woman of the Yelü clan, younger sister of Grand Preceptor Shilu, childhood name Changge.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Yelü clan, sister of Grand Preceptor Shilu, was known by the childhood name Changge.

sentences.zh: 幼爽秀，有成人風。

translations.literal: In youth she was clever and elegant, with the bearing of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: As a child she was bright and graceful, with the poise of a grown woman.

sentences.zh: 及長，操行修潔，自誓不嫁。

translations.literal: When she had grown, her conduct was cultivated and pure; she vowed never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, her conduct was refined and pure, and she vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 能詩文，不茍作。

translations.literal: She could compose poetry and prose and would not write carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: She could write poetry and prose, but would not compose lightly or without purpose.

sentences.zh: 讀《通曆》，見前人得失，歷能品藻。

translations.literal: Reading the Comprehensive Chronicles, whenever she saw the gains and losses of men of old, she could always appraise and classify them.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Comprehensive Chronicles, she could appraise and classify the successes and failures of past rulers whenever she encountered them.

sentences.zh: 咸雍間，作文以述時政。

translations.literal: During the Xianyong era she wrote an essay to set forth current government.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianyong reign she wrote an essay setting forth her views on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「君以民為體，民以君為心。

translations.literal: Its gist said: "The ruler takes the people as his body; the people take the ruler as their heart.
translations.idiomatic: Its gist ran: "The ruler takes the people as his body; the people take the ruler as their heart.

sentences.zh: 人主當任忠賢，人臣當去比周，則政化平，陰陽順。

translations.literal: The sovereign ought to employ the loyal and worthy; ministers ought to remove factional cliques—then government will be made level and yin and yang will be in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign should employ the loyal and worthy; ministers should cast off cliques and factions—then government will be even and yin and yang will be in harmony.

sentences.zh: 欲懷遠則崇恩尚德，欲強國則輕徭薄賦。

translations.literal: If one wishes to cherish those afar, then esteem benevolence and honor virtue; if one wishes to strengthen the state, then lighten corvée labor and reduce taxes.
translations.idiomatic: To win over distant peoples, honor benevolence and virtue; to strengthen the state, lighten corvée labor and reduce taxes.

sentences.zh: 四端五典為治教之本，六府三事實生民之命。

translations.literal: The Four Beginnings and Five Canons are the root of governance and instruction; the Six Storehouses and Three Affairs are the fate of the living people.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Beginnings and Five Canons are the foundation of rule and instruction; the Six Storehouses and Three Affairs are the lifeblood of the people.

sentences.zh: 淫侈可以為戒，勤儉可以為師。

translations.literal: Extravagance may serve as a warning; thrift may serve as a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Let extravagance be your warning and thrift your teacher.

sentences.zh: 錯枉則人不敢詐，顯忠則人不敢欺。

translations.literal: Rectifying the crooked, then people will not dare to cheat; displaying loyalty, then people will not dare to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Set crooked things straight and none will dare to cheat; make loyalty plain and none will dare to deceive.

sentences.zh: 勿泥空門，崇飾土木；

translations.literal: Do not cling to the empty gates, adorning and decking out earth and timber;
translations.idiomatic: Do not cling to the empty gates of Buddhism, lavishing adornment on earth and timber;

sentences.zh: 勿事邊鄙，妄費金帛。

translations.literal: Do not treat the border regions lightly, recklessly wasting gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: do not treat the borderlands lightly, squandering gold and silk in vain.

sentences.zh: 滿當思溢，安必慮危。

translations.literal: When full, think of overflowing; when secure, consider danger.
translations.idiomatic: When the cup is full, think of spillage; when you are secure, reckon with danger.

sentences.zh: 刑罰當罪，則民勸善。

translations.literal: When punishments match crimes, then the people will be encouraged to do good.
translations.idiomatic: When punishments fit the crime, the people are moved toward goodness.

sentences.zh: 不寶遠物，則賢者至。

translations.literal: If one does not treasure distant goods, then the worthy will come.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not treasure exotic goods from afar, the worthy will come to you.

sentences.zh: 建萬世磐石之業，制諸部強橫之心。

translations.literal: Establish the enterprise of the eternal bedrock cliff, restrain the hearts of the various tribes that are overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Build an enterprise firm as bedrock for ten thousand generations, and curb the overbearing hearts of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 欲率下則先正身，欲治遠則始朝廷。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to lead those below, one must first rectify oneself; if one wishes to govern what is far, one must begin at court."
translations.idiomatic: To lead those below, first set your own person right; to govern what is distant, begin at court."

sentences.zh: 上稱善。

translations.literal: The sovereign praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her essay as excellent.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使耶律乙辛愛其才，屢求詩，常哥遺以回文。

translations.literal: At the time the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelü Yixin admired her talent and repeatedly asked for poems; Changge sent him a palindrome verse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelü Yixin admired her talent and repeatedly asked her for poems; Changge sent him a palindrome verse in reply.

sentences.zh: 乙辛知其諷己，銜之。

translations.literal: Yixin knew that it satirized him and bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin knew she was satirizing him and harbored a grudge.

sentences.zh: 大康三年，皇太子坐事，乙辛誣以罪，按無跡，獲免。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dakang, when the heir apparent was implicated in an affair, Yixin falsely charged him with a crime; though investigated with no trace found, he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dakang (1077), when the heir apparent was implicated in a case, Yixin falsely charged him with a crime; the investigation found no evidence, and the prince was spared.

sentences.zh: 會兄適魯謫鎮州，常哥與俱，常布衣疏食。

translations.literal: When her elder brother Shilu was demoted to Zhen Prefecture, Changge went with him, always wearing plain clothes and eating simple food.
translations.idiomatic: When her elder brother Shilu was banished to Zhen Prefecture, Changge went with him and lived always in plain clothes on simple fare.

sentences.zh: 人問曰：「何自苦如此？」

translations.literal: Someone asked, "Why torment yourself in this way?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked her, "Why do you torment yourself like this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「皇儲無罪遭廢，我輩豈可美食安寢。」

translations.literal: She replied: "The heir apparent was innocent yet deposed—how can we of his party eat fine food and sleep in peace?"
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "The heir apparent was innocent yet deposed—how can people like us eat fine food and sleep in peace?"

sentences.zh: 及太子被害，不勝哀痛。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was killed, she was overcome with unbearable grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was killed, her grief was beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 年七十，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy she died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy she died at home.

sentences.zh: 耶律奴妻蕭氏，小字意辛，國舅駙馬都尉陶蘇斡之女。

translations.literal: The wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao, childhood name Yixin, daughter of the State Uncle and Princess Consort Taosuwo.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu, known by the childhood name Yixin, was the daughter of the State Uncle and Princess Consort Taosuwo.

sentences.zh: 母胡獨公主。

translations.literal: Her mother was Princess Hudu.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Princess Hudu.

sentences.zh: 意幸美姿容，年二十始適奴。

translations.literal: Yixin possessed a fine countenance; at twenty she was first married to Nu.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was graced with fine features; at twenty she was first married to Nu.

sentences.zh: 事親睦族，以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: She served kin with harmony toward the clan and was known for filial reverence.
translations.idiomatic: She treated her kin with care and kept the clan harmonious, and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗與娣姒會，爭言厭魅以取夫寵，意辛曰：「厭魅不若禮法。」

translations.literal: Once at a gathering of sisters-in-law they disputed whether witchcraft was better to win a husband's favor; Yixin said, "Witchcraft is not as good as ritual and law."
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a gathering of sisters-in-law, they argued over whether witchcraft was the better way to win a husband's favor; Yixin said, "Witchcraft is not as good as ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 眾問其故，意辛曰：「修己以潔，奉長以敬，事夫以柔，撫下以寬，毋使君子見其輕易，此之為禮法，自然取重於夫。

translations.literal: The assembly asked the reason; Yixin said, "Cultivate oneself to purity, serve elders with respect, attend the husband with gentleness, nurture those below with generosity—do not let gentlemen see one's lightness; this is ritual and law, and naturally one will be honored by the husband.
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, Yixin said, "Cultivate yourself in purity, serve your elders with respect, attend your husband with gentleness, and treat those below with generosity; do not let any worthy man see you behave lightly. That is ritual propriety, and by it you will naturally win your husband's regard.

sentences.zh: 以厭魅獲寵，獨不愧於心乎！」

translations.literal: To gain favor through witchcraft—would one not alone be ashamed before one's heart!"
translations.idiomatic: To win favor through witchcraft—would you not be ashamed before your own heart!"

sentences.zh: 聞者大慚。

translations.literal: Those who heard were greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 初，奴與樞密使乙辛有隙。

translations.literal: At first Nu and the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Nu and Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin had been at odds.

sentences.zh: 及皇太子廢，被誣奪爵，沒入興聖宮，流烏古部。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was deposed, he was falsely accused, his nobility stripped, and he was confiscated into the Xingsheng Palace and exiled to the Wugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was deposed, Nu was falsely accused, stripped of his rank, confined in the Xingsheng Palace, and exiled to the Wugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 上以意辛公主之女，欲使絕婚。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Yixin a daughter of the princess, he wished to make her end the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yixin was a princess's daughter, the emperor wished to dissolve the marriage.

sentences.zh: 意辛辭曰：「陛下以妾葭莩之親，使免流竄，實天地之恩。

translations.literal: Yixin declined, saying, "Your Majesty, owing to my humble kinship by marriage, has spared me exile—that is truly the grace of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin declined, saying, "Your Majesty, because I am kin by marriage, has spared me banishment—that is grace vast as Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 然夫歸之義，生死以之。

translations.literal: Yet the righteousness of a wife following her husband is to live or die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the righteousness of a wife who follows her husband is to live and die with him.

sentences.zh: 妾自笄年從奴，一旦臨難，頓爾乖離，背綱常之道，於禽獸何異？

translations.literal: From the year I pinned up my hair I followed Nu; suddenly meeting hardship and at once being torn apart—to turn my back on the constant way of the norms would make me no different from beasts!
translations.idiomatic: From the day I pinned up my hair I have followed Nu; now, at the first stroke of hardship, to be torn from him at once and turn my back on the constant way—how would that differ from the beasts?

sentences.zh: 幸陛下哀憐，與奴俱行，妾即死無恨！」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty pity me and let me go with Nu together—then even if I die I shall have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will pity me and let me go with Nu, I shall die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved by her words, assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by her words, granted her request.

sentences.zh: 意辛久在貶所，親執役事，雖勞無難色。

translations.literal: Yixin long remained at the place of banishment, personally performing menial tasks; though toilsome, her face showed no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin long remained in exile, personally performing menial labor; though the work was hard, her face showed no distress.

sentences.zh: 事夫禮敬，有加於舊。

translations.literal: In serving her husband with ritual respect, she was even more so than before.
translations.idiomatic: In serving her husband with ritual respect, she was even more devoted than before.

sentences.zh: 壽隆中，上書乞子孫為著帳郎君。

translations.literal: During Shoulong, she submitted a memorial asking that her sons and grandsons be made zhuanglang gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: During Shoulong she submitted a memorial asking that her sons and grandsons be enrolled as registered gentlemen of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其節，召舉家還。

translations.literal: The emperor praised her integrity and summoned her whole family to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her integrity and summoned her entire household home.

sentences.zh: 子國隱，乾統間始仕。

translations.literal: Her son Guoyin began to hold office in the Qiantong period.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Guoyin first entered office during Qiantong.

sentences.zh: 保大中，意辛在臨潢，謂諸子曰：「吾度盧彥倫必叛，汝輩速避，我當死之。」

translations.literal: In Baoda, Yixin was at Linhuang and told her sons, "I judge that Lu Yanlun will certainly rebel—you all flee quickly; I shall die for this."
translations.idiomatic: During Baoda, while Yixin was at Linhuang, she told her sons, "I am sure Lu Yanlun will rebel—you must flee at once; I shall die for it."

sentences.zh: 賊至，遇害。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, she met with disaster and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came, she was killed.

sentences.zh: 耶律術者妻蕭氏，小字訛裏本，國舅孛堇之女。

translations.literal: The wife of Yelü Shuzhe, Lady Xiao, childhood name Eoliben, daughter of the State Uncle and Tribal Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Shuzhe, known by the childhood name Eoliben, was the daughter of the State Uncle and Tribal Chief.

sentences.zh: 性端愨，有容色，自幼與他女異。

translations.literal: Her nature was upright and sincere, with comely countenance; from childhood she differed from other girls.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and sincere by nature, with a comely bearing, she had been unlike other girls since childhood.

sentences.zh: 年十八歸術者。

translations.literal: At eighteen she was married to Shuzhe.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married Shuzhe.

sentences.zh: 謹裕貞婉，娣姒推尊之。

translations.literal: Careful, generous, chaste and graceful; sisters-in-law exalted her.
translations.idiomatic: Careful, generous, chaste, and graceful, she was esteemed by her sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及居術者喪，極哀毀。

translations.literal: When she was in mourning for Shuzhe, her grief and self-destruction were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Shuzhe, her grief and self-mortification were extreme.

sentences.zh: 既葬，謂所親曰：「夫婦之道，如陰陽表裏。

translations.literal: After the burial she said to those close to her: "The way of husband and wife is like yin and yang, outer and inner.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial she said to those close to her, "The way of husband and wife is like yin and yang, outer and inner.

sentences.zh: 無陽則陰不能立，無表則裏無所附。

translations.literal: Without yang yin cannot stand; without outer there is nowhere for inner to attach.
translations.idiomatic: Without yang, yin cannot stand; without the outer, the inner has nothing to which it may attach.

sentences.zh: 妾今不幸失所天，且生必有死，理之自然。

translations.literal: I now unhappily have lost Heaven's ordination for me; yet life necessarily has death—this is principle's nature.
translations.idiomatic: I have now unhappily lost my Heaven-appointed husband; yet where there is life there must be death—that is the nature of principle.

sentences.zh: 術者早歲登朝，有才不壽。

translations.literal: Shuzhe early entered court; he had talent but not longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhe entered court while still young; he had talent but not long life.

sentences.zh: 天禍妾身，罹此酷罰，復何依恃。

translations.literal: Heaven's calamity falls on me, encountering this cruel punishment—what further can I rely upon?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has afflicted me with this cruel blow—what is left for me to rely upon?

sentences.zh: 儻死者可見，則從；

translations.literal: If the dead can be seen, then I shall follow;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead can be seen, I shall follow;

sentences.zh: 不可見，則當與俱。」

translations.literal: if they cannot be seen, then I shall die together with him."
translations.idiomatic: if they cannot be seen, I shall die with him."

sentences.zh: 侍婢慰勉，竟無回意，自刃而卒。

translations.literal: Serving maids urged and encouraged her, but in the end she had no change of mind and killed herself with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Her serving maids urged and comforted her, but she would not change her mind and killed herself with a blade.

sentences.zh: 耶律中妻蕭氏，小字挼蘭，韓國王惠之四世孫。

translations.literal: The wife of Yelü Zhong, Lady Xiao, childhood name Ruolan, fourth-generation descendant of King Hui of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Zhong, known by the childhood name Ruolan, was a fourth-generation descendant of King Hui of Han.

sentences.zh: 聰慧謹願。

translations.literal: Intelligent, clever, careful and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent, clever, careful, and dutiful.

sentences.zh: 年二十歸於中，事夫敬順，親戚咸譽其德。

translations.literal: At twenty she married Zhong; in serving her husband she was respectful and compliant; kinfolk all praised her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty she married Zhong; she served her husband with respect and compliance, and kinfolk all praised her virtue.

sentences.zh: 中嘗謂曰：「汝可粗知書，以前貞淑為鑒。」

translations.literal: Zhong once said to her, "You should have some rough knowledge of books; take former women of chaste integrity as your mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong once told her, "You should gain some rough knowledge of books, and take the chaste and worthy women of old as your mirror."

sentences.zh: 遂發心誦習，多涉古今。

translations.literal: Thereupon she set her mind to recite and study, and ranged widely through ancient and modern works.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon she devoted herself to study and recitation, and ranged widely through ancient and modern writings.

sentences.zh: 天慶中，為賊所執，潛置刃於履，誓曰：「人欲汙我者，即死之。」

translations.literal: In the Tianqing period she was seized by bandits; she secretly placed a blade in her shoe and swore, "Whoever wishes to defile me shall die by this at once."
translations.idiomatic: During Tianqing she was seized by bandits; she secretly hid a blade in her shoe and swore, "Whoever would defile me shall die by it at once."

sentences.zh: 至夜，賊遁而免。

translations.literal: By night the bandits fled and she escaped.
translations.idiomatic: By night the bandits fled, and she escaped.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝召中為五院都監，中謂妻曰：「吾本無宦情，今不能免。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor summoned Zhong to be Chief Superintendent of the Five Tribes; Zhong said to his wife, "I originally had no wish for office, yet now cannot escape it.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the emperor summoned Zhong to be Chief Superintendent of the Five Tribes; Zhong said to his wife, "I never wished for office, yet now I cannot escape it.

sentences.zh: 我當以死報國，汝能從我乎？」

translations.literal: I shall repay the state with my death—can you follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: I shall repay the state with my life—will you follow me?"

sentences.zh: 挼蘭對曰：「謹奉教。」

translations.literal: Ruolan replied, "I respectfully accept your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Ruolan answered, "I respectfully accept your instruction."

sentences.zh: 及金兵徇地嶺西，盡徙其民，中守節死。

translations.literal: When Jin troops overran the land west of the mountains, they moved all the people; Zhong guarded his integrity and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin troops overran the territory west of the mountains and relocated all the people, Zhong held to his integrity and died.

sentences.zh: 挼蘭悲戚不形於外，人怪之。

translations.literal: Ruolan's grief and sorrow did not show outwardly; people found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Ruolan showed no outward sign of grief, and people found it strange.

sentences.zh: 俄躍馬突出，至中死所自殺。

translations.literal: Suddenly she spurred her horse and burst forth, reaching the place where Zhong had died, and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly she spurred her horse and dashed out, rode to where Zhong had died, and killed herself.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳氏以經教二子，並為賢相，耶律氏自潔不嫁，居閨閫之內而不忘忠其君，非賢而能之乎！

translations.literal: Commentators say: Lady Chen through the classics taught her two sons, and both became worthy chancellors; the Yelü clanswoman kept herself pure and did not marry, remaining within the inner quarters yet not forgetting loyalty to her lord—could one do this if not worthy?
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Lady Chen taught her two sons through the classics, and both became worthy chancellors; the Yelü clanswoman kept herself pure and would not marry, yet within the inner quarters she did not forget loyalty to her sovereign—could anyone but a worthy woman do such things?

sentences.zh: 三蕭氏之節，雖烈丈夫有不能者矣

translations.literal: The integrity of the three Lady Xiao—though fierce great men there are who could not accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the integrity of the three Lady Xiao—even fierce-hearted great men there are who could not have matched it.
